title: 5e-review-2: review HRR + similarity + snapshots
description:
## Parent

sutra/83 (5e PRD: health metrics + similarity system)

## What to review

Review HRR integration and similarity capabilities after slices 5e-4, 5e-5, 5e-6, 5e-7 land. The two tracks (health + HRR) are independently complete at this point.

Reviewer focus:
- Are HRR vectors producing meaningful similarity results? Test sutra_similar on real functions — do the results make structural sense?
- Do near-duplicate clusters (pattern families) identify real code repetition? Are there false positives (coincidentally similar but unrelated functions)?
- Is the 0.85 similarity threshold reasonable? Too aggressive (too many families) or too conservative (misses real duplicates)?
- Are health snapshots capturing the right data? Can you drill into per-file history and get useful trends?
- Does the trend tool produce actionable deltas?

## Blocked by

- sutra/88 (5e-4)
- sutra/89 (5e-5)
- sutra/90 (5e-6)
- sutra/91 (5e-7)"

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review (diff 8dffee0..e6172b5, 29 files, +2672/-124):

Verdict: **needs-attention** — do not ship yet.

## Findings

1. **[high] HRR encoding ignores operator tokens** (src/similarity/encoder.rs:35-44)
   `encode_recursive` drops every non-named child. Operators/punctuation are anonymous in Rust/Dart ASTs, so `x + y`, `x - y`, `x == y` can encode identically. Makes 0.85 threshold unable to separate materially different functions → false positives in sutra_similar and sutra_duplicates.
   → Include operator/field-role tokens in structural encoding; add regression tests.

2. **[high] Duplicate families can contain below-threshold members** (src/similarity/duplicates.rs:57-83)
   Single-link clustering unions any pair passing threshold, then returns entire connected component. A-B and B-C can pull A-C into same family even when A-C < 0.85. Reported avg_similarity only counts passing edges, hiding weak internal pairs.
   → Use complete-link or bounded-diameter clustering; compute/report min over all member pairs.

3. **[high] Pattern family detection is quadratic in every parse** (src/pipeline.rs:610-615)
   `find_pattern_families` compares every vector pair unconditionally during parse. On workspaces with thousands of functions → tens of millions of 1024-dim vector scans. No cap, index, batching, or timeout. Can stall indexing on normal monorepos.
   → Move behind bounded background path, or pre-bucket by cheap AST fingerprints/LSH.

4. **[medium] Trend can observe incomplete health snapshots** (src/pipeline.rs:632-646)
   Snapshot aggregate row inserted before per-file/component detail rows, no transaction boundary. Concurrent trend query or mid-write failure → bogus deltas from incomplete snapshot.
   → Write snapshot + details in one transaction, or add completion marker.

## Structural review signals
- Risk score: 0.854
- No DD constraint violations
- Convention violations: test struct naming (PascalCase where snake_case expected), async non-pub method in mcp.rs"

messages.author: agent
messages.text:
Fixed findings 1, 2, 4 from codex review in 25bca13:
- Encoder now includes operator tokens (is_operator filter for +, -, *, etc.)
- Clustering uses complete-link pruning (removes below-threshold transitive members)
- Snapshot writes are atomic (single SQL transaction)

Finding 3 (quadratic pattern families) deferred to sutra/98 (performance review)."
